place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 大比 · 对秦雁
place.en: Chending Temple · The contest · Against Qin Yan

setup.zh: 再上台，对面是名册上排头一个的秦雁：真灵根，六层，剑在背上。她冲你一抱拳：「沈师弟，听说你只有二层。」
setup.en: Back on the stage, facing the one first on the register, Qin Yan: true root, layer six, a sword on her back. She salutes you: "Brother Shen, I hear you're only at layer two."

recap.zh: 你躲了秦雁三十招，一剑也没还，绕回了台心。她袖子里扣着一张雷符，看了一眼台下的孩子，没掏，自己走下了台。
recap.en: You dodged Qin Yan for thirty moves without one back, and circled back to the centre. She had a thunder talisman in her sleeve; she looked at the children below, didn't draw it, and walked off the stage herself.

zh: 名册上排头一个：秦雁，六层。
她没掏那张雷符，自己走下了台。
en: First on the register: Qin Yan, layer six.
Thirty moves. You watch only her feet.
She didn't draw the thunder talisman. She walked off the stage herself.

story.zh: 小满跟着上了台。秦雁道：「沈师弟，听说你只有二层。」小满道：「是。」秦雁道：「我说过，不让。」小满道：「我打不过，会跑的。」秦雁一愣，随即笑了。
story.en: Xiaoman followed her up. "Brother Shen, I hear you're only at layer two." "Yes." "I told you: I won't give way." "If I can't win, I'll run." Qin Yan was startled, then laughed.

exits.means: fights Qin Yan by dodging, never striking back

withdrawn.zh: 秦雁收了剑，退后一步：「再来。」
withdrawn.en: Qin Yan sheathes her sword and steps back. "Again."

story.zh:
这一场，跟孙二狗那一场大不一样。秦雁的剑是真剑，招是真招，一剑一剑递过来，又快又稳，逼得台下的人屏住了气。他爹在黑松岭的山涧边上讲过：天下的鹿，都是先动脚。他跟着爹在山里追过几年鹿，追的时候，眼睛只看鹿蹄子。小满不看她的剑，看她的脚：剑往哪里去，脚先往哪里挪；脚往哪里挪，肩膀先往哪里沉。剑再快，他只看她的脚。他躲得很难看，东一跳，西一滚，有两回简直是连滚带爬，引得台下一阵一阵地笑。可笑着笑着，便有人觉出不对来了：三十招过去，那口剑一回也没碰着他。

有一剑来得太快，他来不及看脚，只得往后一仰，剑尖贴着他的鼻子过去，削下了他额前的一绺头发。那绺头发在半空里飘啊飘，飘到台下，正落在阿禾的小本子上。阿禾低头看了一眼，把它夹进了本子里，面无表情，记了一笔。

又有人觉出一样不对来：他躲来躲去，东一跳，西一滚，滚到后来，脚底下踩着的，是台心。鹿给人追急了，绕一个大圈，还是回到它熟的那片林子里。秦雁的剑把他往台边上赶了三十招，他便绕了三十招，绕回了五块青石板拼缝的那一点上。台角那炷香，只剩一点红了。香到了分不出胜负，谁离台心近，谁赢。

秦雁站住了。她右手的袖子里，一直扣着一张黄纸雷符，从第一招扣到这时候，始终没有掏出来。小满离她只有三步，看得见袖口里露出来的那一角，也看得见她握着符的那只手，指节一点一点地白了。掏出来，他便站不住了；掏出来，这五行台，也站不住了。

她往台下看了一眼。头一排蹲着几个刚进门的小孩子，正张着嘴看她，挤在台沿底下，离那几块青石板，不到一臂。

秦雁把扣着符的那只手，慢慢垂了下去。她把剑收回鞘里，冲小满抱了一抱拳，转过身，一步，两步，自己走下了五行台。那炷香，是在她脚落地以后才灭的。

执事愣了半晌，敲锣：「……秦雁出台。沈小满，胜。」台下静了一静，跟着便有人叫起来：「她自己下去的？」「她让了！」「香还没灭呢！」

执事翻开名册，提起笔，在排头那一行「秦雁」两个字上，画了一道。三年的队，一笔。台下有人叹了口气。人堆里一个嗓子：「你……你把她打下去了？」是孙二狗。他脸色发白，指着台下那个淡蓝衣裳的背影，「秘境里，拿剑鞘把我从坑里拽上来的，就是她。半块干粮，也是她给的。」

小满站在台上，张了张嘴，一句话也答不上来。他赢了。他赢的这一场，是拿一个人的三年换的。

老槐树底下，钱掌柜拿炭条把木板上的名字划得只剩几行：**祁长松　一赔一。马小宝　一赔四。**内门那个七层，一赔三。又在底下写了个「沈」字，写了一半，停住了，想了想，把炭条一搁，在那半个字后头画了一道杠——不收了。有人问他怎么不收，他拨着算盘道：「看不准的，不开。」

秦雁站在台下，低头看了看自己的手，又抬起头来看小满，看了好一会儿。小满走到台边，压低了声音：「师姐，你没输。」秦雁道：「香没灭，我先下的台。规矩上，就是输了。」她看了一眼他垂着的手，低声道：「二层的人，躲不过我三十招。你藏着呢。藏得好。」小满道：「师姐也是。」他看了一眼她的袖口。秦雁的眉毛轻轻一挑，拿左手把袖口按了一按，没接这话，又道：「你那几步，是猎户的步子吧？绕一个圈，回老林子。」小满一怔：「师姐怎么知道？」秦雁道：「我爹也是打猎的。我这个名字，就是他起的——他说雁是天上最难射的东西，一辈子没射着过一只。」

她转身要走，又停住了，背对着他，声音压得更低：「昨天夜里，马小宝在你们屋里拿那面镜子照了一圈，今天一早，满外门都传遍了：今天当着全观，他只照你一个。」她没有回头，「四强，你跟他一个半边。你怀里揣着的，不管是什么，捂紧了。」
story.en:
This bout was nothing like Sun Ergou's. Qin Yan's sword was a real sword, her moves real moves, thrust after thrust, fast and steady, till the crowd held its breath. His father, by the stream at Black Pine Ridge, had told him: every deer under heaven moves its feet first. He'd followed his father after deer in the hills for a few years, and on the chase his eyes watched nothing but the hooves. Xiaoman didn't watch her sword; he watched her feet: wherever the sword was going, the foot moved first; wherever the foot moved, the shoulder dipped first. However fast the sword, he watched her feet. He dodged very badly — a hop here, a roll there, twice practically scrambling on all fours — and the crowd laughed wave after wave. But laughing, some began to sense something wrong: thirty moves gone, and that sword hadn't touched him once.

One thrust came too fast to read her feet; he could only fling himself back, and the point went past the tip of his nose and sheared off a lock of hair from his forehead. The lock floated down and down, off the stage, and landed right on A He's notebook. She glanced at it, tucked it between the pages, and, deadpan, made a note.

Then someone noticed another thing wrong: for all his dodging, a hop east, a roll west, where his feet stood now was the centre of the stage. A deer hard pressed runs a great circle and comes back to the wood it knows. Qin Yan's sword had driven him toward the edge for thirty moves, and for thirty moves he had circled, back to the one point where the five bluestones met. The incense at the corner was down to a single red spark. Incense out with no decision, and whoever stood nearer the centre won.

Qin Yan stopped. In her right sleeve, all along, she had held a yellow paper thunder talisman, from the first move to this one, and never drawn it. Xiaoman was three paces from her; he could see its corner peeping from her cuff, and the hand that held it, its knuckles going white bit by bit. Draw it, and he couldn't stand; draw it, and this platform couldn't stand either.

She glanced below the stage. In the front row crouched a few new little ones, mouths open, watching her, packed against the platform's rim, not an arm's length from the bluestones.

Slowly Qin Yan let the hand holding the talisman drop. She sheathed her sword, saluted Xiaoman, turned, and one step, two, walked down off the Five Elements stage herself. The incense went out only after her foot touched the ground.

The steward sat stunned a good while before he struck the gong: "…Qin Yan leaves the stage. Shen Xiaoman wins." Below, a moment's silence, and then voices: "She walked off?" "She let him!" "The incense wasn't even out!"

The steward opened the register, took up his brush, and drew one stroke through the name Qin Yan on the top line. Three years of queuing: one stroke. Someone below sighed. From the crowd a voice: "You… you knocked her down?" It was Sun Ergou, white in the face, pointing at the pale-blue back below the stage. "In the hidden realm — the one who pulled me out of the pit with her scabbard, that was her. The half ration, that was her too."

Xiaoman stood on the stage and opened his mouth and couldn't answer a word. He had won. And what he'd won it with was someone's three years.

Under the pagoda tree Money-Keeper Qian struck names off the board in charcoal till only a few lines were left: **Qi Changsong, one to one. Ma Xiaobao, one to four.** The inner-court layer seven, one to three. Below it he wrote half the character Shen, stopped, thought, put down the charcoal and drew a stroke through the half-character — not taking bets. Someone asked why. Clicking his abacus: "What I can't call, I don't open."

Below the stage Qin Yan looked down at her hand, then up at Xiaoman, a long while. Xiaoman came to the edge and said low: "Sister, you didn't lose." "The incense wasn't out and I left the stage first. By the rules, that's losing." She glanced at the hand hanging at his side and said quietly: "Nobody at layer two dodges me for thirty moves. You're hiding it. Well hidden." "You too, sister." He glanced at her cuff. Her eyebrow lifted slightly; with her left hand she pressed the cuff down and let that pass. "Those steps of yours — hunter's steps, aren't they? Run a circle, back to the old wood." Xiaoman started. "How do you know, sister?" "My father hunts too. He gave me my name — he said the wild goose is the hardest thing in the sky to shoot; he never hit one in his life."

She turned to go, then stopped with her back to him and spoke lower still: "Last night Ma Xiaobao swept that mirror round your room, and by this morning the whole outer court knew: today, in front of the whole temple, he'd hold it up to you alone." She didn't turn. "In the last four, you and he are in the same half. Whatever you've got in your coat, hold it tight."
